# VASP parser reference data

These numeric fixtures come from the public pymatgen **v2025.6.14** test suite:

- `EIGENVAL.nonspin`: first two complete k blocks of [EIGENVAL.gz](https://github.com/materialsproject/pymatgen/blob/v2025.6.14/tests/files/io/vasp/outputs/EIGENVAL.gz), retaining all 12 bands. Only NKPTS was reduced from 315 to 2.
- `EIGENVAL.spin`: the complete single-k-point [EIGENVAL.ispin2.gz](https://github.com/materialsproject/pymatgen/blob/v2025.6.14/tests/files/io/vasp/outputs/EIGENVAL.ispin2.gz), retaining both channels and all 840 bands. Whitespace in header line 6 is normalized.

`reference.json` stores energies and occupations generated by the pinned [official Eigenval initializer](https://github.com/materialsproject/pymatgen/blob/v2025.6.14/src/pymatgen/io/vasp/outputs.py), executed independently of BandViz with only its I/O and Spin enum adapters. The reference reader has no BandViz imports. Every energy, occupation, coordinate and weight is compared, rather than only comparing shapes. SHA-256 values identify the original compressed source and the fixture text normalized to LF newlines. Tests run offline and do not require pymatgen.

The original project's MIT license is included in `LICENSE.pymatgen`. These are numerical parser fixtures, not validated material benchmarks. Synthetic cases for fractional electron counts, malformed inputs and line-mode sampling live in `test_bandviz_parser.py`.
